steps: Placement & floor support

Level surface that carries the fireplace and venting, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. Never directly on carpet, vinyl or other combustibles except wood: use a full-width, full-depth metal or wood panel.

A level surface able to support the fireplace and venting, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies; allow for the large amount of heat it produces.

  • Fire hazard: don't install directly on carpeting, vinyl or any combustible material other than wood. On carpeting, tile or other combustibles other than wood flooring, set it on a metal or wood panel the full width and depth of the appliance.
  • Above floor level: build a solid, continuous platform.
  • Floor protection in front isn't required; a hearth extension may be combustible. Allow for the hearth finish thickness: the fireplace bottom must be level with the finished hearth extension for the safety barrier to fit. Safety screen B36-PTF2 needs the fireplace 3" above the finished hearth.

Outdoor covered installation

Allowed where the fireplace is protected from direct precipitation. Operation is approved from 40°F to 110°F. The overhang (A) and its width to each side (C) must be at least 1/2 of the roofline elevation (B) above the fireplace base (roofline 10' up: 5' or more). Don't interrupt the continuous insulated building envelope or weatherproof membrane; wire to the outdoor requirements of NECA NFPA 70. Black painted safety barriers are highly recommended outdoors.
Stand-offs & nailing flanges

Form and fit the top stand-off brackets and heat shields before setting the unit in the opening; fit the side nailing flanges for 1/4" clearance to framing. Non-combustible material only in the top stand-off zone.

The top stand-offs set the minimum clearance to the header. Use only non-combustible material in this area for the entire width of the fireplace: no wood or sheetrock.

Top stand-offs (before positioning the unit)

  1. Remove and save the (4) screws holding the stand-off heat shields and brackets on top.
  2. Bend each top stand-off bracket at the perforations, align with the holes in the fireplace top and secure with those (4) screws plus the (4) screws on top of the fireplace.
  3. Form the stand-off heat shields (flange up and to the back) and secure them to the brackets with the (8) screws from the components packet.

Nailing flanges

  1. Remove the (2) nailing flanges from the sides; align them with the holes on the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace, and screw through the slots.
  2. Bend at the perforation until parallel with the fireplace face, never toward it.
  3. Set the framing stud against the small stand-off on the back of the flange and secure with nails or screws.

The flanges give the minimum 1/4" side clearance to framing. Never permanently remove these assemblies. Fitting a trim kit? See Section 4.0 first; it's easier to install with the stand-offs and nailing flanges.
Frame the enclosure
Rough opening 42" H × 36-1/4" W × 15-7/8" D with a single vertical header board; hold every Table 3.1 clearance. Vent pass-throughs need 1" clearance and a wall thimble on horizontal runs.

Rough opening H × W42" × 36-1/4"
Rough opening depth15-7/8" (includes 1/2" typical finish material, flush mount)
  • A single vertical header board is required to maintain clearances to combustibles. Framing must meet local building codes and every clearance in the manual.
  • Cold air transfer area: build the enclosure so cold air can't enter the room, and insulate outside walls.
  • Leave clearance in front for barrier removal, component access, gas line installation and service.
  • Masonry (optional): prepare the foundation for the full masonry load.
  • Metal Fab vent pipe: adapter #4DDA; for rear venting add 3-3/4" to the minimum enclosure depth.

Vent pass-through

  • 1" clearance on all sides of vertical vent pipe; 1" on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe.
  • Measure from the fireplace floor level to the center of the wall penetration; frame the opening so the vent runs level through the pass-through.
  • Horizontal runs through walls need Kozy Heat #700-WPT (walls 4" to 6½") or a wall thimble meeting the 1" top clearance. Don't recess the vent cap into the wall or siding.
  • Wall thimbles and attic insulation shields may be insulated with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136.

Typical top, rear and corner layouts (Figure 3.2, p. 13) and minimum horizontal venting framing (Figure 3.4, p. 16) are drawings only.
Facing, mantel & trim
Attach any trim kit before installing the fireplace. Fit the supplied 37-3/4" × 10-1/2" non-combustible board above the unit and keep combustible trim and mantels to the Figure 4.1 rules.

• Trim kits: #B36-FTK finishing trim, or the exterior trim kit (#B36-081) supplied with and only for barrier #B36-RSF2. Both must be attached before fireplace installation; the top trim panel goes on with the top stand-off brackets.
  • Non-combustible zone: the supplied 37-3/4" × 10-1/2" board overlaps the framing sides 3/4" and the header 1/2". Minimum chamber height for horizontal vent terminations: 45-1/2" with rigid pipe (top or rear), 55-1/2" with flex pipe.
  • Combustible mantel: 3/4" trim from 4-1/2" above the appliance top; a 6" mantel from 8"; then 1" more depth for every 1" of height. With barrier B36-RSF2 only: trim from 1-1/2", 6" mantel from 5".
  • Non-combustible mantel: 6" minimum above the appliance to a maximum 6" depth; then 1" up for every 1" deeper.
  • Adjacent sidewall: 3/4" from the finishing edge of the fireplace; 3" for barrier B36-PTF2.

Finishing

Heat above the unit can crack sheetrock. Use dry, dust-free material; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond), cured per its maker's recommendations; and a high quality acrylic latex primer and finish coat. Avoid flat or light-colored paints.

Safety barrier

The bottom frame piece must be installed for the safety barriers. B36-RSF2 fits inside (upper hood flange into the clips); overlap screens hang on notched tabs in the slots. If the screen has gasket rope, it must contact the appliance or finish to achieve the mantel clearances. Louvered B36-PSF2 / B36-FRSF2 ship in the first notch; match the louver and tab notches to the facing thickness.
Gas line + leak test

½" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector to the ½" control valve inlet; leak-test every connection with soapy water. Built for natural gas: for propane, fit the conversion kit before the log set.

• A qualified person, to local building codes; in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Connect a listed (and Massachusetts-approved) ½ in. tee handle manual shut-off valve and flexible gas connector to the ½ in. control valve inlet. The fireplace comes with a 3/8" × 18" long flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • Run the gas line to the connection point (gas line hole: Figure 2.1, p. 9) without obstructing fan operation. The optional fan kit is easier to fit before the gas line is connected.
  • Pressure-testing the supply above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At ½ psi or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
Propane: the fireplace is manufactured for natural gas. Convert with the kit (MV: OCK-S53A), following its instructions and the authorities having jurisdiction, and finish the conversion before installing the log set.
Termination location
Place the cap to the minimum termination clearances (Canada and US columns) and, for vertical caps, the roof-pitch height table. Never connect to a chimney serving any other appliance.

Vertical cap: minimum height (H) from roof to lowest discharge opening

Flat to 6/121.0 ft
Over 6/12 to 7/121.25 ft
Over 7/12 to 8/121.5 ft
Over 8/12 to 9/122.0 ft
Over 9/12 to 10/122.5 ft
Over 10/12 to 11/123.25 ft
Over 11/12 to 12/124.0 ft
Over 12/12 to 14/125.0 ft
Over 14/12 to 16/126.0 ft
Over 16/12 to 18/127.0 ft
Over 18/12 to 20/127.5 ft
Over 20/12 to 21/128.0 ft

Horizontal cap clearances (Canada / US)

B · window or door that may be opened12" / 9"
C · permanently closed window (recommended, condensation)12"* / 12"*

Clearances are to heat-resistant material (wood, metal), not vinyl: Hussong Mfg. isn't responsible for heat damage from terminating under vinyl soffits, ceilings or overhangs.
Vent exit, restrictor & heat shields

Top exit, or convert to rear (cover plates stay on the unused exit). If restricting, slide the restrictor plate into the 4" exhaust before attaching the vent. Vertical vent heat shield on every top-vent install; horizontal shield with minimum horizontal venting.

Rear vent conversion

The unused vent exit must keep its cover plates. To vent out the back, remove the top cover plate and the 6-5/8" combustion air intake and 4" exhaust collars, remove the rear cover plates, then fit the collars to the rear and the cover plates to the top, checking each gasket (Figures on p. 29-30). Don't proceed with the installation until the conversion is complete.

Restrictor plate

In the components packet; it ships with all inner rings intact (most restriction). Knock out the inner-most ring for less restriction, or all inner rings for the least. Bend the tabs to approx. 80° and slide it into the exhaust pipe on top of the fireplace, tabs pointing toward you, before attaching the vent. It can also be added or modified after installation through the baffle (Section 11.2.2).

Vent heat shields

  • Vertical vent heat shield: must be installed for every type of top venting. Flanges toward the fireplace face; (2) slots to the screw holes in front of the flue outlet; (2) screws. Six holes let you offset it to suit the vent.
  • Horizontal vent heat shield: required with minimum horizontal venting. Bend the (3) hand-tabs and screw them to the (3) holes in the vertical shield; the 1" vent stand-off tab rests on top of the vent pipe.

Then run the vent within the limits on the Venting card, following the vent maker's instructions, and provide a means of visually checking the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
Log set & glass

Convert to propane first if needed. Ember panel in front of the burner, logs B36-1 to B36-7 on their pins, notches and bracket, rock wool embers brushed on, and never over burner ports. Latch the glass and refit the bottom frame.

1. Position the ember panel in front of the burner.
  2. Seat base logs B36-1 to B36-4 on the burner's mounting pins (log numbers are on the bottom of each log).
  3. Set logs B36-5 and B36-6 in the notches on the base logs.
  4. Align log B36-7 with the bracket on the burner and the notch on the ember panel.
  5. Distribute the rock wool embers onto the logs and burner with a stiff bristle brush.
Don't place logs directly over burner port holes: improper placement may affect flame appearance and cause excessive soot on the logs and glass.

Glass & bottom frame

Never operate with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and don't remove it hot. To fit it, set the slots on top of the glass assembly over the firebox tabs, lower the bottom into place and pull the two spring-loaded latches out and up. The bottom frame lifts out of slots on the firebox floor for control access and must be reinstalled to maintain clearances.

Servicing the control board (Section 8.4): never operate without its sealing gasket in place; replace the gasket if damaged.
Wiring & optional controls

The millivolt valve needs no 110-120 VAC; never connect 115V to it. Optional wall switch or thermostat on low-voltage wire to TH and TP-TH, with the rocker switch wires disconnected or the rocker left OFF. Fan kit #B36-075: 110-120V, 14 gauge or better, grounded.

• Standing-pilot units have a black piezo igniter button; electronic-ignition units don't. The gas valve is behind the bottom frame; reinstall the frame afterward to maintain clearances.
  • The millivolt gas valve system does not require 110-120 VAC supply to operate. Never connect high voltage (115V) wire to the gas valve; an optional component connection is for low voltage battery or direct current only, never 120 or 240 VAC.
  • Optional thermostat or wall switch: run low-voltage wires (not included) from the gas valve to a convenient wall near the fireplace and connect them to the top and bottom terminals marked TH and TP-TH (Figure 9.4).
  • Either disconnect the rocker switch wires from the back of the gas valve (Figure 9.3) or leave the rocker switch OFF. If it is ON, the burner runs until the rocker switch turns it off; the thermostat or wall switch won't.
  • Junction box: 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps, hot at all times with no switch in the supply. Ground per local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1.

Optional fan kit #B36-075 (75 CFM)

  1. Shut off the breaker. Remove the safety barrier and log set, the burner assembly and pilot shield, the burner heat shield, and the control board ((8) screws).
  2. Insert the fan through the opening and position it at the back of the firebox; secure with (2) flange nuts. Reinstall the control board.
  3. Bring 110-120V wiring (with ground) through the romex connector to the speed control / receptacle assembly, matching the black (hot), white (neutral) and green (ground) wires to the corresponding wires (Figure 9.5).
  4. Secure the assembly to the electrical box with (2) screws, refit the access panel, attach the temperature control switch to the bottom of the firebox, plug in the fan cord and reinstall everything removed.
A to Bblack (hot) from incoming line · black from speed control
C to Dwhite (neutral) from incoming line · white (neutral) from receptacle
E to Fground (bare) from incoming line · ground (green) from receptacle
G to Hwhite from speed control · black from receptacle

The fan turns on when the switch sensor reaches 110° F and off at 90° F. Move the switch to a warmer spot under the firebox to start the fan sooner, cooler to start it later (unplug the fan cord first). Use code-approved line voltage wiring, 14 gauge or better.
Pressure test & flame adjustment

Check inlet (5" - 10.5" WC NG, 11" - 13" WC LP, with all other gas appliances on) and manifold pressure at the valve taps. Burn 15 minutes, then fine-tune the venturi or restrictor for lazy, yellow flames.

Inlet, tap A · NG / LP5" - 10.5" WC / 11" - 13" WC
Manifold, tap B · NG / LP1.6" - 3.5" WC / 6.4" - 10" WC
Factory venturi opening · NG / LP1/8" / 5/8" open

Table 11.2 (BAY-36-MV). Use a 1/4" I.D. hose; snug the tap screws afterward (don't over-tighten) and confirm each tap reads no pressure. Step-by-step tests: the Inlet and Manifold pressure cards.

Note: the manual gives the propane high manifold pressure as 11" WC on p. 8 and 10" WC in Table 11.2 on p. 57.

Burner venturi (qualified service technician only)

Let the fireplace cool before any adjustment. Flames start blue and turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. If soot is on the glass, check log positioning first; logs must not block burner ports. Slight changes create dramatic results: adjust in small steps, burn at least 15 minutes and let it cool between changes.

Dark, orange flame with black tipsventuri closed too far · open slightly
Short, blue flamesventuri open too far · close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesgas pressure too high · check manometer; or venturi closed too far · open slightly
Lazy, yellow flamesno adjustment necessary
Note: the manual points both ways on the venturi for blue, lifting flames: p. 58 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner (and Table 11.4 says to close it for short, blue flames), while the millivolt troubleshooting chart on p. 63 says to open the venturi slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner.

To adjust: remove the safety barrier, glass frame assembly, log set, back log plate, burner assembly and burner heat shield; loosen the venturi screw, adjust, re-tighten and reinstall everything.

Vent restriction (after installation)

Short, flickeringexcessive draft · add restrictor
Lifting or ghostinginsufficient draft · remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor

Burn 15 minutes first. Reach the 4" exhaust pipe through the baffle ((4) screws). Vertical terminations may show an active, compact flame. If flames keep lifting or ghosting after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent installation, shut off the gas supply and call a qualified service technician.

Service checks

Main burner lights within (4) seconds of the main gas valve opening; the flame safety system de-energizes the safety shutoff in no more than (30) seconds; burner flames steady, not lifting or floating.

panels.title: No spark / pilot won't light
items: No spark at the pilot → piezo igniter not grounded or its wires to the electrode loose; tighten the mounting fastener, repair the connections
Wiring at the back of the electrode igniter disconnected → reconnect
Electrode out of position → set a 1/8" gap to the pilot; metal contact can arc below the electrode and along its wire
Sparks but no pilot → no gas: check for multiple shut-off valves in the supply line and the propane tank

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: Pilot flame not reaching the thermocouple → clean the pilot hood, adjust the pilot flame at the gas valve
Loose thermocouple at the valve → fully inserted, hand tight plus 1/4 turn
Thermocouple reading below 15 millivolts → replace the thermocouple
Thermopile below 350 millivolts at TH-TP and TP → adjust the pilot to envelop it, tighten its connections, or replace it
Frequent outages → pilot shield not installed, or pilot flame too high or too low (clean hood, adjust)

panels.title: Burner won't light or stay lit
items: Lighting instructions not followed → gas control knob at ON, rocker switch ON, or wall switch / remote / thermostat calling for heat
Plugged main burner orifice → remove the blockage
Defective switching device → jumper the switch terminals, then the gas valve terminals, to find the bad switch or wiring
Thermopile wires loose at the valve terminals, or pinched and grounding out
Refractory panels (if installed) not tight against the firebox walls

panels.title: Goes out while running · soot · lifting
items: Pilot and burner go out → no propane, glass frame assembly installed wrong, horizontal vent pitch under 1/4" per 12", defective thermopile or thermocouple
… or inner vent pipe leaking exhaust into the firebox, vent cap blocked, excessive draft (install or modify the restrictor)
Glass sooting → log placement, venturi may need opening slightly, vent cap installation or blockage
Flame burns blue and lifts off the burner → venturi setting, vent cap installation, vent pipe leaks or cap debris

light.title: Lighting the pilot
light.html:
You light the standing pilot by hand, using the gas control knob and the black piezo igniter button.

Smell first, down by the floor too. Smell gas? Don't light anything (see Safety & gas smell). Use only your hand to push in or turn the knob, and never use tools. If it won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it; call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  1. Set any thermostat to its lowest setting.
  2. Turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Take off the safety barrier, then lift the bottom frame up and out of its slots.
  4. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
  5. Wait five minutes for any gas to clear, then smell again near the floor. Smell gas? Stop.
  6. Find the pilot: follow the metal tube from the gas control into the combustion chamber.
  7. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counterclockwise to PILOT.
  8. Push the knob all the way in and hold it while pressing the piezo button repeatedly until the pilot lights.
  9. Keep holding the knob for one minute, then let go. It pops back up and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, start again at step 4.
  10. Turn the knob counterclockwise to ON.
  11. Refit the bottom frame and the barrier, turn the power back on, and set the thermostat.
Knob won't pop back out? Stop and call your service technician or gas supplier right away. Pilot won't stay lit after several tries? Turn the knob to OFF and call them.

controls.title: Turning the flames on and off
controls.html:
Once the pilot is lit and the gas control knob is at ON, the main burner is switched by the ON/OFF rocker switch, or by a wall switch, thermostat or remote control if one was added.

With a wall switch or thermostat

  • Leave the rocker switch OFF so the wall switch or thermostat works properly (unless your installer disconnected the rocker switch wires).
  • If the rocker switch is ON, the burner keeps running until you turn the rocker switch OFF. The wall switch or thermostat can't turn it off.

Flame height and heat

The gas valve has a HI/LO knob. Open the control compartment access panel, then turn the knob counterclockwise toward LO or clockwise toward HI until you like the flame and the heat.

Burner won't come on?

Check that the gas control knob is at ON, then switch the burner on with the rocker switch, or set your wall switch, remote or thermostat to call for heat. Anything beyond that is for a qualified technician.

normal.title: That's normal
normal.html:
Foggy glass

When you first light the fireplace, condensation forms on the glass. It happens with all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time. It helps the paint cure faster.

Ticks and creaks

Metal expands and contracts as the fireplace heats and cools, so you may hear noises. That's normal and doesn't affect how well or how long it works.

Blue flames at first

Right after lighting, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. Lazy, yellow flames are what you want. Flame height and look also vary with the venting and the type of gas.

When to call: if the flames stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips (soot), the burner's air shutter may need adjusting. That must be done by a qualified service technician.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is your job, about once a year. Wait until the glass is completely cool: never remove or clean it hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable spot big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Take off the safety barrier.
  3. Pull the two spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down. Lift the glass up and off the two tabs at the top.
  4. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Put it back: fit the slots on top over the tabs, lower the bottom into place, and pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Put the safety barrier back before you use the fireplace.
Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and don't strike or slam it. Wear protective gloves around broken glass. A licensed or qualified service person should replace it; Hussong Mfg. supplies the glass only as a complete assembly.

off.title: Turning the gas off
off.html:
Day to day, just switch the burner off with the rocker switch, wall switch or thermostat. To shut off the gas to the fireplace itself, for example before service:

  1. Set the thermostat to its lowest setting, if you have one.
  2. If service is planned, turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Take off the safety barrier and lift out the bottom frame.
  4. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF.
  5. Put the bottom frame and the barrier back.

Next time, light it from the start: see Light the pilot.

There is also a separate manual shut-off valve on the fireplace's gas line, fitted by your installer.

pilotout.title: If the pilot goes out
pilotout.html:
Relight it with the full lighting steps (see Light the pilot), starting with the knob at OFF and the five-minute wait.

  • Goes out when you let go of the knob: start again from the OFF step, and hold the knob in for one full minute after the pilot lights.
  • Knob doesn't pop back out when you let go: stop and call your service technician or gas supplier right away.
  • Won't stay lit after several tries: turn the knob to OFF and call your service technician or gas supplier.

The 7-day time-out

Some regions require a 7-day time-out. Ask your dealer whether it applies to your installation. Those fireplaces have a gas valve with a timer set for 7 consecutive days once the pilot is lit. If the fireplace isn't used within the 7 days, the main burner and/or the pilot turn off, but the gas control knob stays where it was (PILOT or ON).

To get it going again, you must cycle the system by hand: follow the lighting steps. Each time the main burner lights during the 7 days, the timer resets to 7 days. It's a standard safety feature of the valve.

Pilot keeps going out on its own? Call a qualified technician: the manual says troubleshooting must be done by one.

fan.title: The fan and house power
fan.html:
A fan kit (#B36-075, 75 CFM) is an option for this fireplace. If yours has one:

  • It runs by itself. It turns on when its temperature switch reaches 110° F and off when it cools to 90° F, as long as the speed control is on.
  • Speed control: turn it counterclockwise until it clicks to switch it off. Turn it clockwise past the click to switch it on at the highest setting, then pick the speed you like while the fan runs.
  • New fireplace? Leave the fan off for the first few hours of burning so the paint cures faster.

What needs electricity

The millivolt gas valve doesn't need 110-120 VAC house power to operate. The fan does: it plugs into a receptacle in the fireplace's electrical box, which is wired to 110-120V. Its cord has a three-prong grounding plug. Never cut or remove the grounding prong.

A qualified service person should vacuum the fan every 6 months. Its bearings are sealed and need no oil.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Hot glass and children

Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The fireplace comes with a barrier that reduces the risk of burns from the hot glass: keep it installed to protect children and others at risk. If it gets damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace. Watch young children closely when they're in the same room.

Everyday rules

  • Never burn wood, coal, paper, cardboard or any other solid fuel in it.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from it. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Don't run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a professional service person. It may need cleaning more often if there's a lot of lint from carpeting, bedding and the like. Keep the area around it clear of anything that burns.

What the service person does each year

  • Vacuums the firebox and checks that the glass latches move freely, with spring tension.
  • Examines the vent system and makes sure combustion and ventilation air flow freely.
  • Cleans the glass and inspects it for cracks, scratches and nicks.
  • Vacuums the burner system and checks gas tubes and connections for leaks.
  • Checks that the pilot flame reaches the thermocouple (part of the flame safety system), cleans the pilot hood and checks millivolt output.
  • Confirms the burner lights within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, the flames are steady, and the safety system shuts off within 30 seconds if the flame fails.

Have the optional fan? It needs vacuuming every 6 months. Your own job is cleaning the glass about once a year.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure · BAY-36-MV
specInlet.html:
NG minimum5" WC (1.25 kPa)
NG recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
NG maximum10.5" WC (2.62 kPa)
LP minimum11" WC (2.74 kPa) recommended
LP maximum13" WC (3.24 kPa)

Table 5.2 (millivolt); Table 11.2 gives the same ranges, 5" - 10.5" WC NG and 11" - 13" WC LP. Table 5.1 beside it is for the BAY-36-LE, not this model.

Inlet test (IN tap, A)

  1. Run all other gas appliances in the house (or at full capacity).
  2. Loosen the IN tap screw counterclockwise and attach a manometer with a 1/4" I.D. hose.
  3. Light the pilot and turn the gas control knob to ON; the burner should not light. Note the reading.
  4. Press the ON/OFF rocker switch ON and check the pressure is near maximum inlet pressure.
  5. Rocker switch OFF, knob OFF; remove the hose and snug the screw clockwise (don't over-tighten).
  6. Relight, knob to ON, and reattach the manometer to verify the tap is sealed (no pressure).
Too high or too low? Contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure. A low pressure can cause a delayed ignition.

Pressure-testing the supply above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve; at ½ psi or less, close its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold (outlet) pressure
specManifold.html:
NG high / low3.5" / 1.6" WC
LP low6.4" WC
LP high11" WC (p. 8) · 10" WC (p. 57)
Note: the heating specifications on p. 8 give the propane high manifold pressure as 11" WC (2.74 kPa); Table 11.2, Pressure Requirements - BAY-36-MV, on p. 57 gives the propane manifold pressure as 6.4" - 10" WC (1.59 - 2.48 kPa).

Manifold test (OUT tap, B)

  1. Light the pilot. Loosen the OUT tap screw counterclockwise and attach a manometer with a 1/4" I.D. hose.
  2. Turn the gas control knob to ON, press the rocker switch ON and note the reading.
  3. Remove the hose and snug the screw clockwise (don't over-tighten).
  4. Reattach the manometer to verify the tap is sealed: no pressure with the rocker switch ON.

Flame height and heat output are set with the manual HI/LO pressure modulator knob on the gas valve (counterclockwise LO, clockwise HI).

specElec.title: Electrical & millivolt system
specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps
Millivolt gas valvedoes not require 110-120 VAC
Thermopile350 millivolts minimum
Thermocouple15 millivolts minimum
Fan kit wiringline voltage, 14 gauge or better
  • AC supply to the junction box: hot at all times, with no switch in it. Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines.
  • Never connect high voltage (115V) wire to the gas valve. The optional component connection is for low voltage battery or direct current only, never 120 or 240 VAC.
  • Optional wall switch or thermostat: low-voltage wires (not included) to the top and bottom terminals marked TH and TP-TH on the gas valve.
  • Ground per local codes, or the National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 or the Canadian Electrical Code CSA C22.1.

Thermopile: remote/thermostat/wall switch or rocker switch OFF, gas valve at PILOT (pilot lit); read at the TH-TP and TP terminals. Thermocouple: disconnect it from the valve, one meter lead on its end and one on its copper wire, then start the pilot while holding the knob in.

conflicts.issue: Propane high manifold pressure: 11" WC (2.74 kPa) in 2.1 Heating Specifications vs 6.4" - 10" WC (1.59 - 2.48 kPa) in Table 11.2, Pressure Requirements - BAY-36-MV (Table 11.1 for the LE also reads 10"). Also shown in step9.

Venturi direction for blue, lifting flames: 11.2.1 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner and Table 11.4 says close the venturi for short, blue flames, while the millivolt troubleshooting chart says open the venturi slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner (Table 11.4 also says open it for lifting/ghosting flames).
Propane rear-vent maximum horizontal run printed as 12" (205mm) in 7.6.4.1.1; elsewhere the manual gives 12" as (305mm), so the inch and metric values disagree.

review.notes: The manual covers both the BAY-36-LE (electronic IPI/CPI) and the BAY-36-MV (millivolt). This guide uses the shared sections plus the MV-only ones (9.2.2, 10.2, 10.2.1, 10.2.2, 11.1.2, 12.2, MV parts list); LE content (battery back-up, IPI/CPI switch, Proflame 2, Tables 5.1/11.1, electronic troubleshooting) is left out. Physical page numbers equal the printed footers; pages 2, 4, 6, 68, 70 are blank. Catalog inputs (26,500 NG / 26,500 LP max) match p. 8; catalog height/width/depth (32", 35.75", 15.8125") match values printed in Figure 2.1 (p. 9), a drawing, so the guide doesn't transcribe dimensions. Not in the manual, so not checked: efficiency (70% NG / 74% LP AFUE), weight (178 lb) and view area (29-7/16" x 23-7/8"; the manual only lists the 26-1/4" x 31-3/8" glass part, p. 67). Catalog feature 'fan kit standard on the log version' vs the manual's '#B36-075 Optional Fan Kit' (p. 50, 67). No remote is described for the MV; the MV chart (p. 62-63) only names a remote, thermostat or wall switch. The MV rocker switch location isn't stated in the text (Figure 9.3 only). p. 63 lists 'knob ON, rocker ON, wall switch/remote/thermostat in heat demand' as remedies while p. 47 says the rocker must be OFF for optional controls; the guide treats them as alternatives. Recorded but not flagged (inch values agree or obvious typos): p. 11 'B36-PFT2' vs B36-PTF2 (p. 10, 19, 67); chamber-height metric values vary (45-1/2" as 1556mm and 1156mm, 55-1/2" as 1410mm and 1156mm, p. 19-20); NG low manifold 0.40 kPa (p. 8) vs 0.41 kPa (p. 57); troubleshooting cites 'Section 11.2.2 Restrictor on page 53' (it is p. 59); p. 39 points to Figure 7.4 for the propane shaded area (the chart is Figure 7.7, p. 40); the rear-vent pages 38 and 40 open with 'For top vent...'; Table 5.2's propane minimum cell reads '11" WC (2.74 kPa) recommended'; the gas line caution cites 'ANSI 223.1' (Z223.1 elsewhere). Pilot flame (Figure 13.2), vent charts (Figures 7.5-7.7), mantel drawings and Figure 2.1 are drawings only. The p. 57 inlet test says to check the reading is 'near maximum inlet pressure', quoted as printed.
